claims.text: Stepwise isothermal aging can control phase evolution in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloys.
The treatment gradually transforms the initial microstructure into a tuned distribution of coherent precipitate phases.
The initial alloy may be an as-cast or homogenized material with either a continuous single B2 phase or a multiphase eutectic microstructure.
An AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy contains FCC and ordered B2 phases.
A lower-temperature aging step around 600 °C induces fine-scale ordered domains.
A subsequent aging step around 750 °C coarsens the ordered domains and changes them toward an off-stoichiometric state.
The proposed sequential 600 °C and 750 °C treatment should be followed by rapid quenching.
A controlled inert atmosphere and precise time-temperature control permit precipitate evolution without over-coarsening.
Aging forms and evolves coherent nanoscale L1₂ or B2-type domains.
The precipitates evolve from perfectly ordered domains with jagged boundaries into larger off-stoichiometric precipitates with smoother interfaces.
Low-temperature aging around 600 °C can produce ordered L1₂ domains and is associated with a ductile-to-brittle transition.
If left unmodified, the low-temperature ordered domains develop into a continuous brittle phase.
The higher-temperature treatment partially disorders the ordered domains and reduces interface energy and stress concentrations.
Partial disordering and smoother interfaces promote dislocation transmission.
Controlling phase volume fractions and interface coherency improves the balance between precipitation strengthening and ductility.
The stepwise-aged alloy should have both higher yield strength and greater ductility than the as-cast or homogenized state.
The treatment should reduce tempering-like embrittlement.
The treatment should produce a more homogeneous microstructure whose fine coherent precipitates improve damage tolerance.
Overaging can cause excessive precipitate coarsening, while insufficient aging may fail to modify the precipitate structure.
Treatment effectiveness is composition-sensitive and may not transfer to alloys far from the target Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni system.
